faqs.question: Do you come directly to my home or office in Peshawar?
faqs.answer: Yes! That is the core foundation of our service: 'We come to you.' You do not need to unplug cables, pack your desktop or laptop into a bag, or navigate busy traffic to drop your PC at a market shop. We bring our diagnostic tools, installation media, and equipment right to your location.

faqs.question: How does the on-site computer service work?
faqs.answer: It's simple: 1) Contact us via WhatsApp or submit our quick online booking form. 2) Explain your PC issue. 3) We agree on a convenient day and time. 4) The technician visits your location, tests the machine in front of you, diagnoses the root cause, and resolves it after your direct approval.

faqs.question: How long does a Windows installation take?
faqs.answer: We focus on fast, thorough installations without cutting corners. On modern computers with an SSD and USB 3.0, clean installation, official drivers, and essential software typically take around 45 to 60 minutes. On older mechanical HDDs, slower processors, or systems requiring large data transfers, it may take 75 to 90 minutes.

faqs.question: Can you move my existing Windows and files from an HDD to a new SSD?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is one of our most popular services! If your current Windows installation and HDD sectors are healthy, we clone your entire operating system, programs, and desktop directly onto the SSD. Your system boots in seconds with all files intact. If the old drive has severe bad sectors or corruption, we advise on safe data backup followed by a clean setup.

faqs.question: Can you recover my deleted or lost files?
faqs.answer: Recovery is possible in many cases, provided the sectors where the files were stored have not been overwritten by new data. We utilize non-destructive drive imaging and recovery software. However, we are completely transparent: if a hard drive is physically damaged (clicking noises, dropped, burnt PCB, head failure), it requires a specialized cleanroom laboratory.

faqs.question: What should I do immediately if I accidentally deleted important files or formatted a drive?
faqs.answer: STOP USING THE COMPUTER IMMEDIATELY. Do not copy new files, do not download software onto that drive, and do not reinstall Windows. Any new data written to the drive can permanently overwrite the deleted sectors. Turn off the computer and contact us right away for an on-site assessment.

faqs.question: Can you fix Blue Screen (BSOD) errors without deleting all my files?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Many repair shops take the lazy approach of immediately formatting your PC for a Blue Screen. A Blue Screen is merely a symptom. We analyze the Windows minidump crash log, test RAM modules with memtest, inspect drive S.M.A.R.T. health, and update faulty drivers to resolve the actual cause while preserving your data.

faqs.question: Do you install pirated or cracked software?
faqs.answer: No. As a Computer Science and Cybersecurity learner, I strictly do not install cracked, keygen, or pirated software. Cracked software frequently bundles trojans, cryptocurrency miners, and backdoor rootkits that compromise your personal data, banking credentials, and system stability.

faqs.question: Can you help if I forgot my Windows account password?
faqs.answer: We provide authorized local account recovery and PIN troubleshooting for verified owners of the computer. For encrypted drives (like BitLocker), access strictly requires the official BitLocker recovery key or authenticated Microsoft Account.

faqs.question: Do you provide bulk Windows installation and setup for offices, schools, and labs?
faqs.answer: Yes. For organizations with 5, 10, 20, or 50+ computers, we utilize standardized imaging and deployment methods so your entire lab or office is configured uniformly with drivers, networking, and software in a fraction of the time. Request a bulk quote through our form or WhatsApp.

faqs.question: Do you bring thermal paste and tools on-site?
faqs.answer: Yes, full diagnostic kits and precision screwdrivers are brought on every visit.

benefits: Instant Boot Times: Windows boots in 10-15 seconds compared to 2-5 minutes on an old mechanical drive.
Faster App Launching: Browsers, Microsoft Office, Photoshop, and IDEs open almost instantaneously.
Smooth File Transfers: High-speed read/write speeds eliminate system-wide freezing and 100% disk usage.
Zero Moving Parts: SSDs are silent, generate less heat, consume less battery power, and resist physical shock.
Less Waiting, More Studying/Working: Eliminates everyday lag during multitasking, browser tab switching, and zooming.
Old HDD can be kept as a secondary storage drive for backups!
problemSolutions.subtitle: Mechanical HDD to High-Speed SSD Upgrade & Migration Pipeline
problemSolutions.title: Make Your Old Computer Feel Faster
problemSolutions.priceStarting: Starting from Rs. 2,000 on-site in Peshawar
problemSolutions.honestAssessment: Direct migration depends on the health of your old drive and existing Windows installation. If the old mechanical drive has failing sectors or severe operating system corruption, a clean setup with manual data migration is much safer and more reliable.
problemSolutions.shortDesc: Many older computers use traditional mechanical hard disk drives (HDDs). Replacing the system drive with a modern SSD is the single highest-impact upgrade you can make to improve everyday responsiveness.
symptomsWhenNeeded: Windows taking 3 to 5 minutes to boot
Task Manager constantly showing 100% disk usage
Frequent browser freezing when opening tabs
Slow file copy and sluggish application launching
Loud grinding or clicking read-head noise from old HDD

warningRules: DO NOT FORMAT THE DRIVE: Formatting destroys file directory tables and sector allocation maps.
DO NOT INSTALL WINDOWS ON IT: Installing a new OS overwrites tens of thousands of sectors permanently.
DO NOT COPY NEW FILES TO IT: Any new document, video, or download takes the space of deleted files.
DO NOT KEEP USING IT UNNECESSARILY: Even normal web browsing writes temporary cache files to the storage drive.
Turn off your computer now if you have deleted crucial files.
problemSolutions.subtitle: Non-Destructive Data Preservation & Sector Carving Protocol
problemSolutions.title: Lost Your Data? Stop Before You Format.
problemSolutions.honestAssessment: We are 100% honest with customers: No on-site technician can fix physically destroyed hard drive heads in a bedroom or office. If your drive has clicking sounds or dead motor, it requires a cleanroom laboratory.
recoverableScenarios: Accidentally deleted thesis, assignments, or documents
Family photos & videos deleted from Recycle Bin
Drive formatted by mistake during Windows setup
RAW partition or "You need to format the disk before using it" error
Windows crashed and refuses to boot, but files remain on drive
Accidentally deleted partition using Disk Management
unrecoverableScenarios: Clicking / grinding metallic sound from HDD
Drive motor completely dead / not spinning
Burnt circuit board / electrical surge failure
Physical head crash or platter scratches

steps.desc: Safely disconnect power or unmount the partition immediately.
steps.title: STOP USING THE DRIVE
ASSESS THE DRIVE
steps.desc: Check S.M.A.R.T. health, read sector availability, and detect physical versus logical damage.
Lock write access using read-only mounting to ensure original drive stays untouched.
steps.title: PROTECT ORIGINAL DATA
CREATE AN IMAGE/CLONE
steps.desc: Bit-by-bit raw disk image cloned to a verified external working drive.
Run deep signature carving and reconstruction on the cloned copy without touching the patient drive.
steps.title: RECOVER FROM THE COPY

problemSolutions.shortDesc: When files are deleted, they may remain physically present on the drive until their storage sectors are overwritten by new data. Acting promptly and properly is the difference between full recovery and permanent loss.

symptomsWhenNeeded: Corrupted Drivers: Outdated or conflicting display, Wi-Fi, or audio kernel drivers.
Failing RAM Stick: Bit-flip errors in memory addresses during intensive tasks.
Failing Storage (SSD/HDD): Bad sectors or controller timeout during OS disk operations.
Thermal Throttling & Dust: Dried thermal paste causing CPU/GPU to overheat and trigger protection shutoff.
System File Corruption: Damaged Windows kernel binaries after sudden power cuts or failed updates.
Hardware Instability: Voltage fluctuations or aging motherboard capacitors.
problemSolutions.title: Blue Screen? Find The Real Cause.
problemSolutions.shortDesc: A Blue Screen is a symptom. Reinstalling Windows is not always the correct solution. If your RAM has a hardware defect or your GPU driver is corrupted, reformatting will simply crash again tomorrow. We diagnose the true root cause.

steps.title: CHECK STOP ERROR CODE
steps.desc: Identify exact kernel stop code (e.g. IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL, KERNEL_DATA_INPAGE_ERROR, CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED)

steps.title: ANALYZE MINIDUMP LOGS
steps.desc: Extract Windows crash dump using WinDbg to pinpoint the specific .sys driver or module that crashed
Run multi-pass hardware RAM stress diagnostic to detect memory cell defects

steps.desc: Examine reallocated sectors, CRC error count, and NVMe health percentage

steps.desc: Monitor real-time sensor temperatures under synthetic stress to rule out overheating
steps.title: THERMAL & VOLTAGE INSPECTION

steps.desc: Replace bad driver, repair corrupt files, or swap faulty component without blindly wiping files
